title: Mixing: Rockestra Theme, The Broadcast by Wings | 1979
content:
Replica Studio, London
Producers: Paul McCartney, Chris Thomas

Paul McCartney oversaw stereo mixes of two songs on Wings’ seventh studio album Back To The Egg on 19 February 1979.

‘Rockestra Theme’ was the first to be tackled, but a final mix proved elusive until the following day.

McCartney turned instead to some of the experimental recordings made the previous year at Lympne (pronounced Lim) Castle in Kent, England. One of the owners, Harold Margary, had recited lines from The Sport Of Kings by Ian Hay and The Little Man by John Galsworthy over an instrumental by Wings. The result was ‘The Broadcast’.

The two people who owned the castle we were recording at … We set up a little mobile unit and they used to invite us in for a drink every evening. Me and Linda would sit in their sitting room and they were [gently upper-class accent] ‘very lovely people, very far back.’ We got a great relationship with them. Even though we were different generations and classes, we just had a lot in common. And I hit on this idea, I asked them would you select some favourite prose or poetry, just read it for me and I’ll use it in a collage. So that became ‘The Broadcast’.

Paul McCartney
Conversations with McCartney, Paul Du Noyer
